title: Tokyo markets fully closed — Labor Thanksgiving Day, and JPX will NOT open derivatives either (group-wide BCP testing), so JGB futures are dark two sessions before the 40-year auction
source: NEWS: jpx.co.jp/english/derivatives/rules/holidaytrading/ — JPX's own derivatives holiday-trading page, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 48,483 bytes) by the jgb-40y-auction-2026-11-25 initial research. Its notes carry, verbatim: 'Markets will not be opened on November 23, 2026 (Labor Thanksgiving Day) due to a JPX Group-wide BCP testing (disaster recovery testing) of FY 2026 which is planned to be implemented for November 21 through 23.' That is an explicit carve-out from the page's own general rule that non-business days are in principle eligible for holiday trading, so 11-23 is a TOTAL Tokyo blackout rather than the cash-only closure a Japanese national holiday normally produces. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED from a second MOF primary and from statute, by the same session: MOF's own JGB par-yield business-day series (jgbs/reference/interest_rate/data/jgbcm_all.csv, HTTP 200, 1,176,385 bytes, 13,296 sessions 1974-09-24 → 2026-08-31) shows a market holiday on November 23 in every year 2015-2023 where the date fell on a weekday, and the substitute Monday (2014-11-24, 2025-11-24) in the two years it fell on a Sunday — exactly the behaviour Japan's Act on National Holidays prescribes for the fixed November 23 Labor Thanksgiving Day. 2026-11-23 is a Monday, so no substitution applies. Filed estimate on the two standing counts: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Discovered during the jgb-40y-auction-2026-11-25 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-09) at D-2 from that auction. NOT a new find to this repo, and that is the point: the jpx-market-closure-2027-03-22 ledger read the same JPX page on 2026-09-05 and explicitly BANKED 2026-11-23 without proposing it — 'Banked but not proposed (six months out of corridor)'. It is now inside a corridor, so it is proposed. Why it earns a row rather than staying banked: the BCP carve-out means the closure reaches the RATES side, which an ordinary Japanese national holiday does not. That sibling ledger established from the same primary that Osaka Exchange normally trades Nikkei index futures and options straight through a Japanese holiday while JGB futures, options on JGB futures and interest-rate futures are ineligible; a 'Not Open' day removes even the equity leg. The consequence for the corridor this proposal was found in: the JGB futures contract that is the hedging and price-discovery instrument for a super-long auction is unavailable on the Monday, and the 2026-11-25 40-year auction therefore prices in a four-session Tokyo week whose first session is gone. The proposing ledger measured whether that matters and found it does NOT at conventional significance — 40-year cover in a holiday-shortened week runs 2.820 (n=19) against 3.044 (n=76), t = -1.69 raw, and -0.168 (t = -1.07) once each auction is compared to its own two neighbours — so this entry is filed as corridor structure, not as a demand signal. Note the pleasing calendar coincidence, which is coincidence and nothing more: Japan's Labor Thanksgiving Day (11-23) and the US Thanksgiving closure (thanksgiving-market-closure-2026-11-26) fall in the same week, so both hemispheres run short weeks around this auction. IMPACT LOW: a foreign-exchange closure moves nothing by itself, no house playbook is calendar- or holiday-keyed, and this repo tracks no Japan-listed symbol. PRECEDENT for the id and shape: jpx-market-closure-2026-12-31 and jpx-market-closure-2027-03-22, both already on this calendar. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
